novel_features.name: Salary distribution over live listings
novel_features.description: Get salary percentiles, a histogram, and the pay-disclosure rate for a role and location by sampling matching listings (which it also caches locally).
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregating salary ranges parsed from many listings — SEEK exposes no salary-aggregation endpoint, and every scraper stops at per-listing fields.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this instead of fetching hundreds of listings and computing pay statistics yourself.

novel_features.name: Hiring-volume trend series
novel_features.description: See how job-listing volume for a classification, region, or work arrangement changes over time, bucketed from the listing dates of every job the CLI has cached, with period-over-period deltas.
novel_features.rationale: Needs the listing-date history the CLI accumulates locally across runs; the API only ever returns a point-in-time count.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when the question is 'is hiring up or down', not 'what is open right now'.

novel_features.name: Company hiring scan
novel_features.description: Profile one advertiser: their company details and review ratings plus every current opening and a local history of how many roles they've posted.
novel_features.rationale: Combines a filtered search, the GraphQL company profile, and a local advertiser-to-jobs join that no single SEEK call returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for 'who is hiring for X' market scans and interview prep instead of scrolling a company's SEEK page.

novel_features.name: Live facet breakdown
novel_features.description: Break a live query down by classification, work type, pay band, or region by tallying the sampled result pages — no local store needed.
novel_features.rationale: SEEK's own facet counts come back empty on the API; this samples the result rows and tallies the chosen dimension in one pass.
novel_features.example: seek-pp-cli listings facets --keywords "data analyst" --where "Brisbane QLD" --group-by classification --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for a fast shape-of-the-market answer before committing to a full search or a sync.

novel_features.name: Classification taxonomy resolver
novel_features.description: Browse or resolve SEEK's numeric classification and subclassification IDs so filtered searches can target them precisely.
novel_features.rationale: SEEK's classification tree is a large numeric taxonomy with no public lookup; this ships it as a curated, facet-refreshed reference.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Call this first when you need a --classification value for listings search.

novel_features.name: New listings across every saved search
novel_features.description: Run every one of your SEEK saved searches and return only the postings that aren't already in your local store, tagged by which search matched.
novel_features.rationale: Orchestrates your authenticated saved searches, a per-search query, and a local anti-join against everything you've already seen — no endpoint does this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: This is the daily-driver command for an active job hunt; use it instead of re-scrolling the SEEK site.

narrative.headline: Every SEEK search and job-detail feature, plus a local job history, salary distributions, and hiring trends no other SEEK tool has.
narrative.value_prop: seek-pp-cli searches Australian and New Zealand job listings, pulls full job details through SEEK's own JSON endpoints (never the bot-gated HTML), and keeps every job it has seen in a local SQLite store. On top of that it computes salary percentiles (salary), hiring-volume trends over time (trends), per-company hiring scans (company), and runs all your saved searches for new postings in one command (me new-jobs). No API key; no hosted scraper.
narrative.auth_narrative: Job search, job details, salary data, and company profiles need no authentication. The me commands (saved searches, saved jobs, applied status) read your SEEK session: run `seek-pp-cli auth login --chrome` once while logged in to au.seek.com in Chrome and the CLI imports the session cookie. Nothing is written to your SEEK account.

troubleshoots.symptom: listings get or a company scan returns nothing for a valid job ID
troubleshoots.fix: SEEK's GraphQL schema may have shifted; re-run with --json to see the raw error, then trim the query fields the error names.

troubleshoots.symptom: me new-jobs or me saved-searches says you are not authenticated
troubleshoots.fix: run `seek-pp-cli auth login --chrome` while logged in to au.seek.com in Chrome; only the me commands need this.

troubleshoots.symptom: salary or trends shows a thin distribution or no history
troubleshoots.fix: these commands accumulate listings locally on each run; run the same query a few times over days, or widen --where / drop filters for a bigger sample.

troubleshoots.symptom: search returns AU jobs when you wanted NZ

narrative.when_to_use: Use seek-pp-cli when an agent needs to search or monitor Australian/NZ job listings, pull structured job details, compute salary statistics, or track hiring volume over time. It caches every job it fetches to a local SQLite store, so salary and trends answer aggregate questions the SEEK site and every scraper cannot.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to submit a job application or edit a SEEK profile/resume — it is read-only against your account.
Do not use it for job boards other than SEEK (Indeed, LinkedIn, JobStreet non-AU/NZ) — it only speaks to au.seek.com.
Do not use it for the SEEK partner/hirer Job Posting API (developer.seek.com) — that is a different, credentialed product.
